question: An object with a mass of 10 kg is moving with an initial velocity of 3 m/s and its final velocity becomes 5 m/s. Then the change in its kinetic energy is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**80 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The change in kinetic energy is calculated using the relation:

 **ΔKE = (1/2) m ( vf² − vᵢ² )**
 
• Here, **m** is the mass, **vf** the final velocity, and **vᵢ** the initial velocity.
 
• Substituting the given values:

 **ΔKE = (1/2) × 10 × ( 5² − 3² )**
 
• This becomes:

 **ΔKE = (1/2) × 10 × ( 25 − 9 )**
 
• Simplifying further:

 **ΔKE = 5 × 16**
 
• Therefore:

 **ΔKE = 80 J**
 
• The change in kinetic energy is **80 joules**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• **Kinetic Energy**__

 __
 
• Kinetic energy is the energy an object possesses due to its motion.
 
• It is given by **KE = (1/2) m v²**.
 
• The SI unit of kinetic energy is the **joule (J)**.
 
 
 
• **Mass**__
 
 
• Mass is the measure of the amount of matter in a body and is measured in kilograms (kg).
 
• It is a scalar quantity and remains constant irrespective of location.
